itinerary.title: Quy Nhon - Mang Den
activities:
Morning: A coach and guide pick up guests in Quy Nhon, and the group departs for Mang Den to explore the great Central Highlands.
Guests experience the climb over An Khe Pass. From the vehicle, guests can freely take in the majestic mountains and forests of the Central Highlands and admire the spectacular winding pass roads. The guide organises activities to connect everyone on board.

11:00: Arrive in Mang Den. The group has lunch at a restaurant with local highland specialties.
Afterwards, check in at the hotel/homestay and rest.
15:00: The group begins exploring famous Mang Den landmarks:
•	Thac Pa Sy Tourist Area: Walk through poetic pine forest paths, admire the pristine Pa Sy waterfall sending white foam through the valley, and visit the unique folk wooden statue area.

•	Toong Dam Lake Tourist Area: Admire the calm, cool lake surface, stroll around the shore to see seasonal flowers (peach blossoms, purple flamboyant flowers, etc.), and immerse yourself in the peaceful atmosphere of the highlands.
•	Check in at Sunset Boulevard: The group visits a beautiful sunset viewing road. Here, guests are free to watch the sun set behind the old pine trees and take memorable photos.
18:00: Guests move to dinner with local specialties.

Evening: Guests are free to stroll around town and explore the food scene or relax at cafes. 
(Dinner and personal services are at own expense.)
Overnight in Mang Den.

itinerary.title: Mang Den - Quy Nhon
activities: Morning: Guests have breakfast at the hotel.
07:45 – 08:00: Vehicle and guide pick up guests for sightseeing.
Mang Den Mother Mary – one of the important and famous religious symbols in Mang Den – and learn about the spiritual story behind it.
Enjoy coffee: Find a peaceful little cafe corner amid the pine forest and sip a cup full of Central Highlands character.
Stroll and shop: Visit local markets to buy specialties as gifts (dried bamboo shoots, wild ginseng, forest honey, etc.).
11:00: The group checks out of the accommodation and then moves to a restaurant for lunch.

13:00: Leave Mang Den town and visit Kon Pring Village – a cultural village of the M'Nam people amid the great Mang Den forest, known for its traditional stilt houses, communal house, and simple, peaceful local cultural life.

14:00: Say goodbye to Mang Den, and the vehicle departs for Quy Nhon.
Afternoon (expected 16:30-17:00): Arrive back at the original pickup point in Quy Nhon. The guide says goodbye and concludes the highland journey.

tour_qn_4n3d.title: Quy Nhon 4 Days 3 Nights
overview: Quy Nhon is an ideal destination for nature lovers and those who love exploration. It attracts visitors with clear blue water, fine white sand, magnificent rocky headlands, and wild, poetic beauty.

In Quy Nhon, visitors can admire Ky Co – a beautiful island paradise, explore Eo Gio – a natural masterpiece amid the vast sea and sky, and find peace at Cu Lao Xanh Pearl Island. Each destination has its own colour, opening up a journey full of interesting and memorable experiences.
Beyond its natural scenery, Quy Nhon also captivates visitors with a rich coastal cuisine, fresh seafood, and distinctive local culture.
highlights: Ghenh Rang Tien Sa: A green pearl in the heart of Quy Nhon
Twin Towers: An ancient Cham tower complex with unique architecture.
Cu Lao Xanh: The Pearl Island of the Far East
Ky Co: 'Vietnam's Maldives'.
Eo Gio: A walking path hugging the coastal cliffs.

Stroll leisurely on the romantic Mong Cam slope and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere.

16:30: Continue to Twin Towers – a unique ancient Cham architectural work with historical and artistic value, one of the typical cultural marks of Binh Dinh.
17:30: Visit Nguyen Sinh Sac – Nguyen Tat Thanh Square, a work of historical and cultural significance expressing deep father-child affection and the patriotic tradition of the Vietnamese people.

itinerary.title: QUY NHON – CU LAO XANH
activities: Morning: Have breakfast at the hotel.

07:00 – 07:30: A coach and guide pick up guests at the meeting point in central Quy Nhon, depart for Mui Tan Pier, and board a speedboat to begin the journey to Cu Lao Xanh Pearl Island. During the 20-30 minute crossing, guests can enjoy the vast panorama of Quy Nhon Bay, breathe the fresh sea air, and take souvenir photos at sea.
08:30: Arrive at Cu Lao Xanh island; a shuttle takes guests to the restaurant to rest and enjoy a refreshing cold lemon drink after the sea crossing.
09:00 – 11:30: Begin exploring the impressive destinations on the island:

Conquer Cu Lao Xanh Lighthouse – one of Vietnam's top 5 famous lighthouses more than 100 years old. Standing proudly on the mountain top, the lighthouse is a beautiful symbol of the enduring vitality and resilience of the island commune's fishermen.

Check in at Thao Nguyen Rock Beach – home to hundreds of naturally arranged rocks in countless unique shapes. The wild, poetic scenery here is loved by many young travellers and compared to the setting of the film 'Descendants of the Sun'.

Enjoy Coral Beach / South Beach: A photo paradise with countless unique angles. Guests are free to swim and experience beautiful coral snorkelling at Bai Nam, Bai Da Hon, Bai Nho, or Bai Thon Dong (free equipment: diving mask, life jacket).
12:00: Return to the restaurant to shower, rest, and enjoy a lunch of fresh seafood rich in island flavours.
14:00: A shuttle picks up guests and returns to the speedboat pier; the group heads back to mainland Quy Nhon.
15:00: Transfer guests back to the hotel to rest and explore Quy Nhon freely.
Evening: Guests are free to stroll around town and explore the food scene or relax at seaside cafes. (Dinner and personal services are at own expense.)

art_an_gi_o_qn.title: What to eat in Quy Nhon: dishes worth trying

body.text: Quy Nhon's food revolves around fresh seafood and side dishes with the bold flavours of Central Vietnam. Prices can vary by season and by vendor, so ask before you order.
Morning

art_di_chuyen_qn.title: How do you get to Quy Nhon?
art_di_chuyen_qn.excerpt: Comparing plane, train, and coach travel to Quy Nhon, with notes on travel time and distance to the centre.

body.text: There are three main ways to reach Quy Nhon. Each suits a different kind of trip in terms of time and budget.
By plane
The fastest option, best when you have only a few days. Phu Cat airport is about 30 km from the city centre, so allow extra time for the transfer by car.
By train
Dieu Tri station lies on the North–South line. The train suits you if you want to take in the scenery along the way and do not mind a long journey.
By coach
Flexible in terms of departure times and pick-up points, but the journey is longer. Choose a sleeper coach for the long haul.

body.title: About combining Quy Nhon and Phu Yen
body.text: If you visit both provinces, decide in advance where you fly in and out to avoid returning to your starting point.

art_ghenh_da_dia_bai_xep.title: Ghenh Da Dia and Bai Xep in one day
art_ghenh_da_dia_bai_xep.excerpt: How to fit Phu Yen's two signature sights into a single unhurried day, with suggested timings.

body.text: Ghenh Da Dia and Bai Xep are fairly close together, so it is entirely possible to visit both in one day if you plan the timing well.
Morning: Ghenh Da Dia
Arrive early, as the area is quite exposed and the sun climbs quickly. Take care walking on the rocks, since the surface can be slippery.
Afternoon: Bai Xep
Bai Xep is smaller and more pleasant in the afternoon. It is also a suitable stop to rest and eat seafood nearby.

items: Midday: lunch in the Dam O Loan area.
Afternoon: Bai Xep, then back to your accommodation.

body.title: Safety on the rocks
body.text: Do not stand too close to the water's edge when the sea is rough. The basalt rocks can be slippery after rain.

art_kinh_nghiem_qn_py.title: Quy Nhon – Phu Yen travel tips for first-time visitors
art_kinh_nghiem_qn_py.excerpt: A round-up of what to know before a trip to Quy Nhon – Phu Yen: when to go, how to get around, which places to see, and how to plan your itinerary.

body.text: Quy Nhon and Phu Yen sit side by side, about 100 km apart by road. That is why the two are often combined in a single trip, even when you only have three days.
When should you go?

The South Central Coast has two fairly distinct seasons. The calm-sea period is usually favourable for island trips and snorkelling; during the rainier and stormier period, it is better to prioritise mainland sites.

body.title: Note on the rainy season
body.text: Itineraries with sea activities should be checked against the weather before departure. Operators usually have alternative plans if the sea is rough.
Getting to Quy Nhon

items: Plane: Phu Cat airport is about 30 km from central Quy Nhon.
Train: Dieu Tri station lies on the North–South line.
Coach: many routes from southern and northern provinces.

body.text: Places worth making time for
Ky Co – Eo Gio cluster
This is Quy Nhon's most famous cluster, suitable for a full day. You should get to the beach early for clearer water and to avoid the strong sun.
Ghenh Da Dia and Bai Xep

These two sites are in Phu Yen and are often combined in half a day. Ghenh Da Dia stands out for its layered basalt columns; Bai Xep has two rock slabs jutting into the sea that are easy to recognise.

body.alt: Layered basalt columns at Ghenh Da Dia
body.caption: Ghenh Da Dia — Phu Yen's geological highlight.

body.text: Suggested three-day itinerary

items: Day 1: Ky Co – Eo Gio, overnight in Quy Nhon.
Day 2: transfer to Phu Yen, visit Ghenh Da Dia – Bai Xep – Dam O Loan.
Day 3: catch the sunrise at Mui Dien and return to Quy Nhon.

body.title: Small tip
body.text: If you have four days, add a morning on the island instead of squeezing in another mainland stop. A slower pace is more enjoyable.

art_thoi_diem_qn.title: When is the best time to visit Quy Nhon?
art_thoi_diem_qn.excerpt: An analysis of the pros and cons of each period of the year so you can choose the right time for your kind of trip.

body.text: There is no single answer to the question 'which month is best for Quy Nhon', because it depends on whether you want to swim, go to the islands, or just stroll around the city.
If you want to go to the islands and snorkel
Prioritise the calm-sea period. This is the most important condition, because boats and speedboats may be postponed when the sea is rough, regardless of your advance booking.
If you want to avoid the crowds
Major holidays usually push up room rates and crowd the beaches. Travelling a few days outside the holiday period usually gives a much more pleasant experience.

body.title: Don't just look at the temperature
body.text: The sun in Central Vietnam is quite strong at midday. Even if the forecast is not very hot, you should still schedule outdoor activities for early morning and late afternoon.
How to check before finalising your dates

items: Check the weather forecast about a week before departure.
Ask the operator about alternative plans if the sea is rough.
Choose a hotel with a clear refund/cancellation policy if travelling in the rainy season.
